criteria.title: Clean Architecture and Solution Organization
criteria.description: The solution uses the .slnx format (or .sln on an older SDK) and contains four projects (Domain, Application, Infrastructure, and Api) with unidirectional dependencies in the correct direction. Domain has zero PackageReference entries. The Application layer is organized into feature folders (Vertical Slices) rather than by technical type. Each layer has its own DI registration method (AddApplicationServices and AddInfrastructureServices) called from Program.cs. The solution builds with zero errors (dotnet build).

criteria.title: Rich Domain Model and Invariants
criteria.description: All eight entities and three enums exist with the required field names (Guid IDs and UTC timestamps). Setters are private, and creation and modification happen through factory methods and entity methods. The ValueObject base class compares by value, accompanied by at least one Value Object such as Money. All ten invariants in SRS §4.5 are modeled in the Domain: inside the entities, invariant 10 as an entity method (such as Category.EnsureCanBeDeleted) that receives the query result from the handler, and invariant 9 via ISoftDeletable and soft delete. DateTime.UtcNow is never called inside the Domain; the current time is passed as a parameter.

criteria.title: Persistence Layer: EF Core, Fluent API, and Migrations
criteria.description: AppDbContext exists, each entity has a separate IEntityTypeConfiguration class registered via ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly, and Data Annotations are not used for mapping. Relationships are configured properly (Category → Campaigns with Restrict, Campaign → Donations, and User → Campaigns and Donations), decimal precision for monetary fields is configured, and appropriate indexes are defined. RowVersion is configured as a concurrency token on Campaign. The initial migration is committed to the repository and applies cleanly to SQL Server.

criteria.title: Generic Repository, Unit of Work, and Read/Write Separation
criteria.description: The IGenericRepository<T> and IUnitOfWork interfaces are defined in Application and implemented in Infrastructure. Write operations go through the Repository and UoW and are persisted with a single SaveChangesAsync call per operation. Read queries use AsNoTracking and project directly to DTOs. Filtering executes on IQueryable in the database rather than in memory.

criteria.title: Soft Delete and Global Query Filters
criteria.description: The ISoftDeletable interface exists, and SoftDeleteInterceptor converts Deleted state to IsDeleted = true while recording DeletedAtUtc. The interceptor is registered on DbContext. The HasQueryFilter excludes deleted records, and IgnoreQueryFilters is used only where necessary (such as checking for associated campaigns before deleting a category).

criteria.title: Options Pattern and Secrets Protection
criteria.description: The JwtOptions, SeedAdminOptions, and DonationOptions classes exist with their required default values, have Data Annotations, and are registered with ValidateOnStart. The application fails fast on startup if any required setting is missing or invalid. Services read configuration via IOptions<T> rather than IConfiguration directly. appsettings.json contains placeholders only, and no secrets (JWT key, passwords, real connection string) exist in the repository or Git history.

criteria.title: Identity & Authentication: JWT and Refresh Token Rotation
criteria.description: Requirements IDN-01 to IDN-12 work: registration with the Donor role, password policy, case-insensitive duplicate email rejection (Auth.EmailAlreadyExists — 409), and login returning a 15-minute Access Token (configurable) containing the required claims. Refresh tokens are stored hashed only; on every refresh, the old token is revoked and linked to the new one and cannot be replayed; an invalid, expired, or revoked token returns Auth.RefreshTokenInvalid (401). Logout revokes the token, GET /auth/me works, and a deactivated user is blocked from logging in or refreshing (Auth.AccountDeactivated — 403). Login returns a generic error message (Auth.InvalidCredentials) whether the email or password is wrong. The seeded Admin is created from options (along with the three roles), the two development test users (Campaign Manager and Donor) are seeded in the development environment only using credentials from user-secrets, and POST /admin/staff works for Admin only. Protected endpoints return 401 without a token.

criteria.title: Categories Module
criteria.description: Requirements CAT-01 to CAT-04 work: creating, updating, and deleting are Admin-only, while listing and retrieving are available anonymously. The name is required in both Arabic and English, max 100 characters, and unique per language. Deleting a category associated with campaigns returns 409 Category.HasCampaigns, and a missing category returns 404 Category.NotFound. The entire API (Categories and Identity) returns DTOs rather than entities, and controllers are thin with no business logic. Development seed data includes five bilingual categories.

criteria.title: API Documentation, README, and Submission
criteria.description: Scalar (or Swagger on .NET 8) works and supports entering a Bearer Token to test protected endpoints. The README documents prerequisites, Migrations commands, setting secrets via dotnet user-secrets, and testing instructions, and includes a Design decisions section justifying read/write separation. The sprint-1 tag exists and points to the final commit, and any fixes are tagged sprint-1-fix without moving the original tag.

criteria.title: Explaining Architectural Decisions and Trade-offs
criteria.description: During review, the learner's ability to explain the rationale behind their decisions, alternatives, and trade-offs between each choice and its alternatives—such as why writes go through a Repository while reads do not, the difference between an Entity and a Value Object, why the Refresh Token is stored as a hash, DI service lifetimes, and why wrapping EF Core queries in Task.Run is prohibited. Answers are evaluated on comprehension rather than memorization.
